newsitem.title: JAPAN: Fuji Heavy 96/97 profits seen larger than expected.
newsitem.headline: Fuji Heavy 96/97 profits seen larger than expected.

text.p: Japan's Fuji Heavy Industries Ltd is expected to post larger profits this fiscal year than the car maker had anticipated, helped by good demand for its sport-utility vehicles, analysts said on Wednesday.

They said the parent current profit of Fuji, which makes Subaru brand cars, would be around 28 billion yen or more for the year ending this month, compared with the company's November estimate of 26 billion yen.
In 1995/96, its actual profit totalled 10.11 billion yen.
Fuji Heavy, owned 4.2 percent by Nissan Motor Co Ltd, will announce actual earnings for 1996/97 on May 22.
"I am just reviewing my estimate of Fuji Heavy's profit. It will be better than my earlier estimate of 27.50 billion yen," Nikko Research senior analyst Noriyuki Matsushima said.
The launch of the new Forester sport-utility car, good demand for its mainstay Legacy model at home, and a recovery in its U.S. unit's profit were behind the better profit estimate.
The buoyant demand is also a factor in the recent rally in the company's shares, he said.
The company's shares have risen 26 percent so far this year, closing at 589 yen on Wednesday after touching an intraday high of 597 yen, their highest level since November 1990.
The shares were helped by Wednesday's news that the Forester model was exceeding the firm's sales target.
Nomura Research analyst Seiji Sugiura said he forecast the company's parent current profit would be 28 billion yen, given the recent good orders for its new Forester model.
"The good profits will likely make the company's shares a good buy until next summer," he added.

Fuji Heavy said on Wednesday it had received 4,000 domestic orders for its new Forester vehicle in the first 20 days after its launch. The company introduced the Forester four-wheel-drive SUV on February 13 in Japan with a monthly sales target of 3,000 units.

Fuji Heavy's domestic car sales including mini cars in the 10-month period to January rose 0.4 percent to 264,400 units from the same period a year earlier. Sales of its profitable Legacy model meanwhile grew 7.6 percent to 71,000, while its vehicle exports rose 44 percent, industry data showed.
Sugiura, however, warned that the current euphoria may not last too long.

Bigger domestic rivals -- Toyota Motor Corp and Nissan Motor Co Ltd, are set to start denting Fuji sales from around next summer by introducing similar models to the Legacy station wagons, Sugiura said.

"Fuji's profit for 1997/98 depends on its domestic sales of profitable Legacy models...at a time when overall domestic demand is expected to fall in and after April due to a planned sales tax hike," Matsushima said.

If rival makers' station wagons go down well, then Fuji Heavy may face a tough sales situation as it has no plans to launch new models for the rest of this year. Sugiura said Fuji Heavy's current profit could fall to 20 billion yen in 1997/98. -- Mitsuo Suzuki, Tokyo Equities Desk (+81-3-3432-8017)
